meaning_fixes.reason: Source is 'kono ryounin no shi to bousou' - one death (Adroc's, row 8879, Summer of Love) and one rampage (Saotome's Shin Dragon / Deuteron Missile incident, row 8880), attributed jointly to 'these two [people]', not two deaths and multiple rampages. The draft's plural 'these two deaths and rampages' implies Saotome also died, which contradicts row 8876 (Saotome immersed himself in further research afterward, i.e. survived). Singular 'that death and that rampage' keeps the one-each reading without changing tag order or newline count.

checked_decisions.finding: Entire block has no <ab()>/<ed()> timing commands anywhere in the source, unlike surrounding combat rows; verified this is a genuine source property (not a draft omission) and that the scene's resource id changes from 6260 to 6261 immediately after row 8891. Preserved as-is; no commands added or removed, consistent with the constraint to keep commands identical and in source order.

English clause order rearranged from a literal reading so each row's <book()>/<color()> tag order matches the source's left-to-right order exactly (e.g. 8862: Dewey, New Federation, Coralians). Spot-checked each against the source; meaning unchanged by the reordering.

'To answer for my crime as his brother, Dewey was imprisoned' - verified against source ('jittei de aru ore no tsumi no sekinin o torasare'): the speaker (Holland) describes himself as Dewey's actual younger brother, so 'his brother' correctly refers back to Dewey (Holland is younger, per franchise canon and row 8858's admission of deserting with Eureka). Not a pronoun error; left as drafted.

'...hides something that Bloodman shouldn't know about' for 'shiranai hazu da' (Bloodman presumably/surely doesn't know) - the English is ambiguous between an epistemic and a deontic reading, but context (Bloodman being kept in the dark) resolves it the same way either way; not a meaning error, left as drafted.

'Michiru' (no surname in the source line, as drafted) checked against the batch's glossary proposal (batch_08856_glossary_proposals.json): Michiru Saotome, Dr. Saotome's late daughter, Getter Robo Armageddon, sourced to the Getter Robo Wiki. This is a different franchise character from Eureka Seven's cast (the exposition block crosses over Getter Robo terms - Getter Rays, Shin Dragon - with Eureka Seven's Ageha Plan/Scub Coral material), consistent with the game's multi-series roster seen in terms_028.json/character_names_021.json. 'Michiru' accepted per orchestrator ruling.
